newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks sink lower in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks sink lower in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks fell steadily in early Friday morning trade, with investors chiefly concerned that a uptick in U.S. employment would force a near-term interest rate hike, brokers said.
"I think alot of people will be on the sidelines today," said Stanley Ng, research manager at Mansion House Securities. "It (the U.S. unemployment figures for February) is a pretty important number."
The Hang Seng Index eased from the open to trade 85 points lower at 13,331 after 30 minutes of trade. Trading was active with HK$1.45 billion in turnover.

"Economists' estimates of U.S. unemployment rates for February are traditionally well wide of the mark and this adds to current market uncertainty," said Kieren Hung, vice president at G.K. Goh Securities.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average eased 1.15 points to 6,944.70, following a drop in U.S. jobless claims to 310,000 prompted caution and fears that the February unemployment report would show a further decline.
Hang Seng index futures also fell sharply in early trade, with the March contract 102 points lower at 13,338 and the April contract 105 points down at 13,340.
Brokers said there was also concerned that the government would take action to curb residential property price rises, thus capping the upside for property stocks.
"Both the PRC (People's Republic of China) and Legco (the Legislative Council of Hong Kong) think further price rises would have a bad impact on society," said a broker with a Japanese house.

Cheung Kong is rumoured to have sold a limited number of new units in its latest luxury residential development project for HK$10,000 per sq f to HK$11,000 per sq ft, about 30 percent above analysts' forecasts.
The property sector led the market down, with developers taking the greatest beating.
Sun Hung Kai Properties slumped HK$1.75 to HK$88.75, Henderson Land slipped HK$1.00 to HK$68.75 and Cheung Kong dropped HK$0.75 to HK$75.00.
Trade in H share China Eastern remained active, with the share gaining HK$0.04 to HK$1.91.
Guangdong Kelon slipped HK$0.15 to HK$7.20.
